summary: Big Shippagan Lighthouse at Shippegan Gully, New Brunswick: first lit in 1872; the present octagonal tower dates from 1905 and is a Coast Guard light.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. The dirt road is rough after 0.8 km; the last 0.9 km (0.6 miles) is on foot.

corrections.why: The 1872 wooden tower was replaced. The 1905 Department report says the old light 'has been replaced by a new and much higher tower', and the tower standing now is 51 feet (16 m) high. The record gives 1872 with the 16.1 m height that the Coast Guard list gives for the present tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 'Fl W 20s' from an older source (not read here). The Coast Guard list gives LFl W 6s for the present light, and the facts use it. LighthouseFriends reports the 1907 change from fixed to single-flashing light.

notes_for_editor: Spelling: the Coast Guard list (entry 1254, Admiralty H1530) prints 'Big Shippagan' and 'Shippegan Gully'; LighthouseFriends and the Parks Canada designation title print 'Big Shippegan'; the 1905 report prints 'Shippigan'. The story uses the Coast Guard form for the light and the common town spelling Shippagan. Keepers: the 1872-1902 keeper LighthouseFriends names is the same as the 1901 Department table; the 1902, 1903 and 1906 tables confirm Robichaud and Savoie by OCR position in the same column line. Keepers 1904 to 1937 come from LighthouseFriends only and were not checked against Department tables for 1907 to 1921 (the corpus tables are split into column blocks). Mrs. A. Robichaud has no first name in any source. Focal height: the record gives 5.0 m with no source. The 1905 report gives the 1906 light as elevated 53 feet (16 m) above high water. The present focal height is not in the Coast Guard text read, so no correction is proposed. Range: the record gives 13 nautical miles, matching the Coast Guard list. Lens: the 1905 report gives a fourth-order dioptric light; LighthouseFriends says a third-order lens came in 1907, but the present lens order is not confirmed by a source read here. 1872 tower: the only source read for the 1872 tower is LighthouseFriends (it quotes Harding's 1871 report and the Department's reports, which are not in the corpus for 1871-1899). Treat its 1872-1883 details as secondary. Heritage: the Parks Canada page renders only its title in this reader, so the 1992 designation date in the record is not verified. The Canadian Register excerpt names Gordon Fulton, Federal Heritage Building Review Office Building Report 90-099, as its source; the report was not read. Automation: no source read says when the light was automated. The Coast Guard list says year round. Access: LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower closed, and that the Coast Guard owns the site. Check before publication, and confirm with the Coast Guard whether the tower is closed to the public now. Not used: the 1000towns travel listing (it repeats LighthouseFriends), the Wikipedia articles (Chiasson-Savoy in French gives 1905 to 1906, leads only), and a community Facebook post on the first tower of 1872. The record's French name Phare de Village-Chiasson appears in its source list (Wikimedia Commons) and was not read. Storms and wrecks: LighthouseFriends records only the October 1879 storm at the station. The drowning of the three brothers preceded the light and is kept in The place. OCR notes: 'Honore Duguay, of Garaquet' in the 1905 report is printed here as Caraquet, the town's usual spelling. 'Savon' in the 1906 table is Savoie. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story no longer says the Acadian Peninsula (not in any source; LighthouseFriends puts the light on Lameque Island). Units now run metres first for this Canadian station. The 1905 report scan (37) prints 'Garaquet' for Duguay's home; Caraquet is cited to LighthouseFriends. Open: the keeper table names for fiscal 1901, 1902 and 1906 (scans 258, 242, 180) were matched from the OCR text on the same line as the station; the page images were not viewed. The spelling 'Savon, Adelard' on scan 180 needs checking against the image. The cached LighthouseFriends page garbles the accent in 'Stanislaus Hach' (the accent is unconfirmed; the story writes Hachè).
